name: Billy Graham
title: Billy Graham: a life devoted to proclaiming Jesus Christ
description: The story of Billy Graham, his evangelism from 1949 onward and the limits of his relationship with power, drawing on sources from BGEA and PBS.

sections.heading: A preacher before a new audience
paragraphs: In 1949, an evangelistic campaign in Los Angeles gave Billy Graham a visibility that would change his ministry. He was not yet the international figure many people remember. He had grown up on a farm in North Carolina and, according to his official biography, had responded to the Christian message during Mordecai Ham’s meetings in 1934.

Ordained in 1939, Graham studied at the Florida Bible Institute and at Wheaton College. In 1943 he married Ruth Bell. His work with Youth for Christ took him to preach beyond his local surroundings. The Billy Graham Evangelistic Association, founded in 1950, later extended that work through radio, television and public campaigns.

sections.heading: A public message and a story that calls for nuance
paragraphs: The BGEA biography presents the proclamation of the gospel as the center of his life’s work. PBS also documents his closeness to presidents and his influence on American life. Both perspectives help us read his story: that of an organization that preserves his legacy, and that of a historical examination of his public decisions.

Graham began to desegregate his campaigns in the 1950s, but his relationship with the civil rights movement had its tensions. The PBS research records his disagreements with Martin Luther King Jr.’s direct protests. Acknowledging that limit allows us to value his evangelism without presenting every political decision as exemplary.

reflection: In 1 Corinthians 2:1–5, Paul places the center of preaching in Jesus Christ crucified and in trust in the power of God. That passage guides our reading of Graham: a preacher’s importance is measured by the message he proclaims, and his fame never replaces the testing of that message in the light of Scripture.

For the church today, his story sets out two inseparable tasks: to communicate the gospel clearly and to guard the independence of Christian witness in the face of prestige and power. We can learn from a long career and also from its tensions. Gratitude for a ministry leaves room for honest questions about its decisions.
review_note: Institutional audience figures are not presented as verified conversions. The historical limits regarding race and political power are retained.
